invariants: The same feature id has the same behavior, state names, failure semantics and accessibility contract in every AI Core consumer regardless of country, team or implementation language.
Products may vary branding, density, icon family and domain copy, but may not fork interaction semantics or completion meaning without a registered exception.
Top is informational and bottom is actionable for task-level actions unless a documented platform or accessibility exception applies.
Every asynchronous action separates request-started, authoritative completion, failure and retry or receipt states.
Every data surface defines loading, empty, error and populated states before it is considered complete.
New reusable UI/UX functionality must be added to this registry before adoption; unregistered common behavior is not a new local standard.
product_owned: Content density within readability and touch constraints
Localized tone of voice and domain labels
Business-specific priority among already valid actions
internationalization: Use explicit language metadata and explicit text direction metadata.
Support both LTR and RTL layouts; direction is a script or content property and is not inferred solely from locale.
Use locale-aware date, time, number and currency presentation while keeping canonical stored values locale-neutral.
Do not concatenate translated UI sentences from fragments where word order may vary.
Allow long labels and translated text to wrap without losing action meaning.
exceptions: Exception must identify feature id, product, reason, owner, verification evidence and expiry or review date.
Accessibility, data integrity, authority and completion-proof requirements cannot be waived by visual preference.
Temporary exceptions do not create a second standard and must not be copied into other products.

rules: Native HTML semantics first; custom widgets implement the equivalent WAI-ARIA APG role, state and keyboard contract.
Default, focus-visible, active, disabled and busy are distinct states; meaning is never color-only.
Product touch target baseline is 44 CSS px unless a documented platform/accessibility exception applies.
Every form control has a persistent visible label; placeholder text is not the only label.
Validation identifies the field, explains correction and preserves entered values.
Required, invalid, disabled and read-only are conveyed semantically and visually.
Top app/page header is informational by default; task CTAs belong in the bottom action area.
One primary action per action boundary; destructive actions are visually and semantically separate.
A disabled action exposes the blocking reason near the action.
Loading, empty, error and populated are specified independently.
Stable row/entity identity is required; refresh and retry must not silently change selection.
Large data defines pagination or virtualization and exposes result count.
Writes are bound to a stable entity/work key and reject stale responses.
Retry is idempotent or otherwise protected against duplicate completed writes.
Recoverable user input survives retry, navigation and transient network failure.
Focus enters the overlay, remains inside a modal boundary and returns to the invoker on close.
Escape closes dismissible overlays; task actions belong in the overlay footer.
Background content is inert only when the overlay actually behaves modally.
Behavioral IDs and state machines are locale-neutral; human copy is localized separately.
Language and text direction are explicit metadata; direction is not inferred solely from language.
Dates, times, numbers, currency, names and addresses use locale-aware formatting/parsing without hard-coded separators.
Engine-facing UI uses queued, running, partial, succeeded, failed and cancelled semantics.
Starting a job is never displayed as successful completion.
Progress, result receipt, retry eligibility and last verified time are explicit.
Adapter-facing UI distinguishes disconnected, connecting, connected, syncing, degraded and error.
Last successful sync, current source and retry path are observable.
External side effects require an explicit completion receipt; opening an external app is not completion.
Mobile is not a scaled desktop; hierarchy and task order stay stable while layout adapts.
No essential action depends on hover.
Sticky/fixed UI must not obscure focused content and must account for safe-area and virtual keyboard.

features.title: Primary action
rules: Use for the single highest-priority immediate action in its boundary.
Label begins with the action verb and names the immediate outcome.

features.title: Secondary action
rules: Visually quieter than primary but equally reachable by keyboard and touch.

features.title: Destructive action
rules: Names the affected object and consequence before irreversible execution.
Requires explicit confirmation when reversal is difficult or impossible.

features.title: Icon-only action
rules: Requires an accessible name and visible help when meaning is not obvious.

features.title: Navigation link
rules: Use links for navigation and buttons for actions.

features.title: Overflow action menu
rules: Secondary or rare actions may move here; the primary task action may not.
Opening and closing restores focus predictably.

features.title: Text input
rules: Use purpose-appropriate autocomplete and inputmode where applicable.

features.title: Number input
rules: Separate canonical numeric value from localized display formatting.
Do not silently round or clamp without exposing the rule.

features.title: Money input
rules: Currency code or unit is explicit and not inferred from symbol alone.
Store numeric amount and currency separately.

features.title: Phone or email input
rules: Allow international formats and preserve country information during normalization.

features.title: Textarea or memo
rules: Multiline content preserves line breaks and draft state.
Autosave exposes saving, saved and error without stealing focus.

features.title: Search field
rules: Opening search must not destroy current work state.
Closing search restores prior list or screen context where practical.

features.title: Select
rules: Prefer native select for short single-choice lists.
Required selection starts with an explicit unselected state.

features.title: Combobox or autocomplete
rules: Implements APG combobox keyboard and focus semantics.
Editable, select-only or suggestion-only behavior is declared explicitly.

features.title: Checkbox
rules: Preserve native checkbox semantics.
Use mixed only when a meaningful partial state exists.

features.title: Radio group
rules: Use when exactly one option from a small visible set is required.
Group has a programmatic label.

features.title: Switch
rules: Reserved for settings that take effect immediately.
Do not use for deferred form submission choices.

features.title: Date input or picker
rules: Stored date semantics are separate from localized display.
Picker has a keyboard path and does not require dragging.

features.title: Time input or picker
rules: Time zone context is explicit when it affects meaning.
12 or 24 hour display does not alter stored semantics.

features.title: Date range
rules: Start and end ordering is validated and explained.
Range shortcuts never hide the actual selected dates.

features.title: File upload
rules: Allowed type, size and count constraints are visible.
Each file has independent progress and result; retry does not duplicate a completed upload.

features.title: Image upload and gallery
rules: All available images remain addressable and representative image is explicit metadata.
Preview, removal and reordering preserve stable image identity.

features.title: Reorder or drag
rules: Every drag interaction has a non-drag single-pointer and keyboard alternative.
Order changes are announced and cancellable before commit where practical.

features.title: App or page header
rules: Header is informational by default: brand, title, context, progress and passive status.
Task CTAs do not move into the header merely to save space.

features.title: Breadcrumb
rules: Represents hierarchy, not history; current location is programmatically exposed.

features.title: Tabs
rules: Implements APG tab semantics including Arrow, Home and End keys.
Selected and focused are distinct states.

features.title: Bottom navigation
rules: Used for top-level destinations, not per-page task CTAs.
Safe-area padding is mandatory on edge-to-edge mobile layouts.

features.title: Pagination
rules: Current page is exposed and unavailable directions are disabled.
Changing page preserves relevant filters and query context.

features.title: Stepper or wizard
rules: Back, Next and Complete belong to the bottom action area.
Single-choice auto-advance omits a redundant Next button.

features.title: Back and state restore
rules: Back restores meaningful prior query, filter, scroll and draft state.
Fallback never silently discards unsaved work.

features.title: List
rules: Interactive row hit areas can exceed visual density.
Selection survives refresh when the entity still exists.

features.title: Card
rules: Make the whole card interactive only when the entire card has one clear destination or action.

features.title: Status badge
rules: Status text accompanies color and vocabulary comes from the domain state machine.

features.title: Table
rules: Use semantic table markup for relational rows and columns.
Narrow screens preserve horizontal scroll or use a documented mobile transformation.

features.title: Sort
rules: Sort state is programmatically exposed and stable in the query contract.
Server or client sorting source is explicit.

features.title: Filter
rules: Applied filters are visible and removable; reset differs from closing without applying.
Filter, facet and result list read the same query snapshot.

features.title: Virtualized or infinite list
rules: Stable item identity and accessible position/count survive mount and unmount.
Loading more never steals focus or unexpectedly resets scroll.

features.title: Detail sections
rules: Section title hierarchy remains consistent between list and detail families.
Read-only and editable are explicit states.

features.title: Definition or key-value list
rules: Use semantic name/value grouping and allow long localized labels to wrap.

features.title: Source or SSOT provenance
rules: Show source, revision or observed-at time when source identity affects trust.
Unknown source fails closed for state-changing decisions.

features.title: Audit trail
rules: Events are append-oriented, timestamped and actor or source attributable.
Human-readable summaries do not replace immutable event identifiers.

features.title: Inline validation error
rules: Error is adjacent or programmatically associated and explains correction.

features.title: Alert or banner
rules: Urgent blocking errors use alert semantics; routine status uses polite announcement.
Critical information persists until resolved or intentionally dismissed.

features.title: Toast
rules: Only confirms background-safe completed actions and never holds the sole copy of critical information.
Does not steal focus.

features.title: Progress indicator
rules: Progress represents real job state and respects reduced-motion preferences.

features.title: Skeleton loading
rules: Skeleton approximates layout without implying actual data values.
Screen-reader verbosity is controlled.

features.title: Empty state
rules: Explains why nothing is shown and offers the next valid action when one exists.

features.title: Retry pattern
rules: Retry preserves recoverable input and follows idempotency and receipt rules.

features.title: Modal dialog
rules: Use only for a focused task that must be completed or dismissed before continuing.

features.title: Bottom sheet
rules: Preferred mobile secondary action or filter surface when it avoids top-header CTAs.
Gesture dismissal has a button and keyboard equivalent.

features.title: Drawer
rules: Use for supplementary navigation or context, not hidden mandatory form steps.
Focus and scroll locking match explicit modal or non-modal intent.

features.title: Tooltip
rules: Supplementary only; essential instructions never exist only in a tooltip.
Available on keyboard focus as well as pointer hover.

features.title: Draft preservation
rules: Draft is bound to a stable work or entity key and is never confused with server completion.

features.title: Autosave
rules: Debounced or background saves expose state and do not overwrite a newer revision silently.

features.title: Explicit save
rules: Save is bottom-positioned and success appears only after authoritative persistence.

features.title: Submit or complete
rules: Submission is a distinct boundary from draft save and names the externally visible effect.

features.title: Delete
rules: Confirmation names object and consequence; restore semantics are explicit if supported.

features.title: Undo
rules: Undo window and scope are explicit and never imply reversibility beyond backend capability.

features.title: Optimistic update
rules: Optimistic UI stays distinguishable until authoritative confirmation when failure matters.
Rollback restores prior known state without losing unrelated edits.

features.title: Concurrent edit conflict
rules: Never silently last-write-wins where data loss is material.
Expose base and current revisions with a deterministic resolution path.

features.title: Offline or degraded network
rules: Queued writes are not displayed as completed.
Reconnect reconciles by stable IDs and revisions.

features.title: Permission and read-only
rules: Hide or disable according to policy without exposing unavailable sensitive data.
Unknown permission fails closed for mutation.

features.title: Session expiry and re-auth
rules: Preserve recoverable draft state across re-authentication.
Protected mutations require renewed authority after expiry.

features.title: Engine job status
rules: Every long-running engine task exposes stable job id, progress or result, retry eligibility and receipt.

features.title: Adapter connection
rules: Connection health is observable independently from the last successful operation.

features.title: Sync
rules: Sync shows source, target, observed revision or time and conflict policy.

features.title: Import
rules: Validate and preview before commit when mutation is material.
Per-record failures remain inspectable and re-runnable without duplicating successes.

features.title: Export
rules: Export names format, scope and snapshot or revision.
Generated files expose expiry and security semantics when needed.

features.title: External action or deep link
rules: Launching phone, SMS, mail or a third-party app is not completion.
Completion requires a receipt or remains explicitly unverified.

features.title: Document preview
rules: Preview preserves file identity and version and exposes a safe fallback action.
Unsupported formats fail explicitly.

features.title: AI-assisted action
rules: AI output remains draft or candidate until the product authority boundary accepts it.
Model execution and application commit are separate states.

features.title: Notification
rules: Queued, sent and delivered stay distinct when the provider exposes them.

features.title: Webhook or event delivery
rules: Event id and delivery attempts are stable; retry policy prevents duplicate side effects where possible.

features.title: Responsive behavior
rules: Content order and task priority remain semantically stable across layout changes.

features.title: Localization and text direction
rules: Layout supports long translated copy, RTL direction and locale formatting without changing business behavior.

features.title: Focus management
rules: Focus is visible, logical and not obscured by sticky or fixed content.

features.title: Safe-area and virtual keyboard
rules: Bottom actions remain reachable and content or focus is not hidden by safe-area or virtual keyboard.
